key_insight: Nutri-ATLAS combines a nutrition knowledge graph, LLM reasoning, and robot-based evidence gathering to make food and meal recommendations more reliable in real-world settings.
clinical_relevance: It could help support personalized nutrition planning by better handling ambiguous foods, missing nutrient data, and patient-specific constraints like allergies.
method: Builds a unified Food-Nutrient knowledge graph from USDA FoodData Central and FoodKG.
Learns 64-dimensional GATv2 food and recipe embeddings for graph-text retrieval.
Uses an embodied agent with LLM-guided skills to inspect food availability and update context memory.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong benchmark results, including 37.9% MAP on HealthyFoodSubs, 78.8% MAP on PFoodReQ, and successful adherence to allergy and healthy-target constraints in a patient-profile study.
watch_item: Performance is benchmark-strong, but real-world deployment may still depend on the quality, coverage, and upkeep of the nutrition graph, robot sensing, and LLM hardware constraints.
paper_title: Nutri-ATLAS: Embodied Agent for Tabulated Lookup and Assistance for Smarter nutrition
